Please let us know your preferred location in advance. If you require hotel pick-up from Tokyo or another area outside Kamakura or Fujisawa, or would like to arrange a private vehicle, we can provide a custom quote based on your departure point.

route.title: Engaku-ji — Zazen Meditation: A Stillness Held in Half-Light
route.body: Engaku-ji ranks second among Kamakura's Five Mountains, the great Zen temples of the old shogunate. Here, your guide will lead a short zazen meditation — not a full formal session, but enough to experience, even briefly, what the practice asks of you: stillness, breath, and attention.
route.titleJa: 円覚寺 — 座禅 — 薄暗がりに満ちる静けさ
route.bodyJa: 円覚寺は鎌倉五山の第二位に列せられる禅寺です。ここでは、ガ イドとともに短い坐禅を体験していただきます。本格的な修行で はありませんが、静けさと呼吸、そして意識を澄ますという禅の 感覚を、気軽に味わっていただけます。

route.title: Jochi-ji — Discovering Wabi-Sabi: The Quiet Beauty of Zen
route.body: Jochi-ji, the fourth of the Five Mountains, keeps its grounds simple — a bamboo grove, moss-covered stone steps, and flowers that change with the seasons. There is little to do but walk slowly, let your senses settle, and take in the scenery as it unfolds.
route.titleJa: 浄智寺 — 侘び寂びの発見 — 静寂なる禅の美
route.bodyJa: 鎌倉五山の第四位、浄智寺は、境内を飾らずに保っていま す。竹林、苔むした石段、季節ごとに移ろう草花——ここで は、ただゆっくりと歩き、五感に耳を澄ませながら、目に映 る景色をご堪能ください。

route.title: Zen Lunch — Shojin Ryori or Your Choice
route.body: Enjoy traditional shojin ryori (Zen Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) or a lunch tailored to your preferences, arranged in advance as part of the experience.
route.titleJa: 禅ランチ — 精進料理またはお好みの昼食
route.bodyJa: 本格的な精進料理、またはお客様のお好みに合わせたお食事をお楽しみください。（ランチは料金に含まれております）

route.title: Jomyo-ji — A Bowl of Matcha, Served in Quiet
route.body: Jomyo-ji, ranked fifth among the Five Mountains, is home to a beautiful tea house set quietly within its grounds, overlooking a dry landscape Zen garden raked into rippling lines. Here, matcha is served in quiet, with the garden doing the talking.
route.titleJa: 浄明寺 — 静けさの中でいただく、一服の抹茶
route.bodyJa: 鎌倉五山の第五位、浄妙寺の境内には、美しい日本茶屋がひっそ りと佇んでいます。目の前には、波紋のように掃き整えられた枯山水。静けさの中でいただく一服の抹茶は、庭がすべてを語って くれます。

ledeParasEn: Kamakura has preserved its temples for 850 years — and its stillness for just as long.

This tour is built around that stillness: not a rapid checklist of sights, but an unhurried journey through three of Kamakura's Five Great Zen Temples. Your guide brings their history to life while giving you time to slow down and absorb each place.

The Five Mountains, or Kamakura Gozan , are five of the city's most important Rinzai Zen temples, whose foundations were laid during the Kamakura shogunate and later ranked among the highest in the temple hierarchy under the Muromachi shogunate: Kencho-ji, Engaku-ji, Jufuku-ji, Jochi-ji, and Jomyo-ji.

On this journey, experience a brief zazen meditation at Engaku-ji, stroll through the seasonal grounds of Jochi-ji, and savor matcha overlooking the dry landscape Zen garden at Jomyo-ji. The morning concludes with a relaxed lunch tailored to your taste.
Everything is arranged in advance. All you need to bring is a willingness to slow down.
For full-day tours, the afternoon itinerary following lunch is fully customized to your preferences.

円覚寺では短い坐禅を体験し、浄智寺では四季折々の草花が彩る境内をそぞろ歩き、浄妙寺では枯山水を眺めながら抹茶をいただ きます。午前の締めくくりには、お好みに合わせたお店で昼食を。すべての手配はあらかじめ整えてありますので、あとはゆっくりと歩む心構えだけをお持ちください。終日ツアーをご予約のお客様は、昼食以降の行程をオーダーメイドでご提案いたします。

ledeParasEn: ZENRISE designs slow, considered private experiences around Kamakura and its surrounding towns.
This private experience offers an intimate introduction to ikebana with working ikebana master Koen Yokoi, arranged for one to six guests in a quiet setting.
The Japanese phrase ichigo ichie — one time, one meeting — expresses the idea that each encounter is unique and can never be repeated in quite the same way.

The flowers you see, the arrangement created by the master, and the time shared together form a moment that exists only once. At the end of the experience, you can take your finished arrangement home as a keepsake of your time in Kamakura.
Koen Yokoi

Koen Yokoi was born into a family with three generations of connections to the performing and floral arts. Her grandfather was Kuro Hosho Shigehide, the 17th head of the Hosho School of Noh. Her father, Shigeru Yokoi, was a Noh stage director and choreographer, while both her grandmother and mother were ikebana artists of the Sogetsu school.

After graduating from Musashino Art University, she inherited the family's ikebana practice in 2000. Since 2001, she has designed floral installations for film sets, Noh stages, embassies, and public spaces in Japan and abroad.
Widely known for her cherry blossom installations, she also advocates for a more eco-conscious approach to ikebana.
ledeParasJa: Zenriseは、鎌倉とその周辺の街を舞台に、ゆっくりと考え抜かれたプライベート体験を企画しています。
本体験は、現役の華道家による、少人数だけのための生け花体験です。1名から6名までの少人数限定で、静けさを大切に選ばれた部屋にて行います。
「一期一会」という言葉は、二度と同じようには訪れない、たった一度きりの出会いを表します。その日の朝に切られた花、生け花マスターの手で、この小さなグループのためだけに生けられる一枝。仕上がった作品はそのままお持ち帰りいただけます。二度と同じ形では訪れない出会いの記憶として。

生け花マスター横井紅炎は、能楽宝生流17世宗家・宝生九郎重英を祖父に、舞踊演出家の横井茂を父に、そして祖母・母ともに草月流華道家という家に生まれた。武蔵野美術大学卒業後、2000年に家督を受け継ぎ、2001年より能舞台、現代劇、コンサート、公共空間、デモンストレーションなど、日本国内外のあらゆる空間に花を生けてきた——本人いわく「空間へチャレンジしていく」仕事である。「桜花いけ請負人」としても知られ、廃棄素材や採集した自然物を用いるエコ推進華道家としても活動している。

ledeParasEn: A quiet moment with a flame can become one of the most memorable parts of a journey.

In Shonan, discover the traditional craft of Japanese candle-making through an intimate workshop led by local candle artisan Meria. Working with natural materials sourced from the region, you will shape your own Japanese candle entirely by hand.
Limited to four guests, the experience takes place in a quiet setting in Kamakura or Fujisawa — a chance to slow down, work with your hands, and experience a different rhythm of Japan.
Your finished candle is yours to take home, carrying with it the memory of your time in Shonan.
Shonan Japanese Candles
Inspired by the quiet beauty of the Shonan coast, Shonan Japanese Candles bring together local materials and a traditional Japanese craft.

Each candle is made by hand from plant-based mokurō wax, derived from the Japanese wax tree, with a natural wick made from washi and rush. As the candle burns, the wax is drawn into the wick and gradually disappears into the flame, leaving very little residue.
The natural materials allow the candle to return gently to the environment. Its larger, steady flame has long been valued in Japanese temples and tea rooms.
Meet Meria
Based in Fujisawa, Meria creates Shonan Japanese Candles using natural materials from local farmers and producers.

From developing each color to shaping and finishing every candle, she works entirely by hand, choosing a slower process over mass production. Her workshops offer a space to become absorbed in the simple act of making — where time seems to slow, and the hands take over.
ledeParasJa: 炎を静かに見つめる時間は、旅の中でも心に残るひとときになることがあります。
湘南で活動する蝋作家・Meriaとともに、日本の伝統的な和蝋燭づくりを体験します。地域の自然素材に触れながら、一本の和蝋燭をすべて手作業で仕上げます。定員4名までの少人数制。鎌倉または藤沢の静かな空間で、手を動かしながら、いつもとは少し違う日本の時間を味わいます。完成した和蝋燭は、そのままお持ち帰りいただけます。湘南で過ごした時間を思い出す、小さな灯りとして。
湘南和蝋燭について

湘南の海辺の静かな美しさと、日本の伝統技法をひとつの灯りに込めた「湘南和蝋燭」。日本の和蝋燭は、ハゼの実から採れる植物性の蝋「木蝋」と、和紙やイグサでつくられた自然素材の芯から、一本ずつ手作りされます。火を灯すと、蝋は芯に吸われながらゆっくりと燃え、最後には炎の中へと消えていきます。蝋垂れや燃え残りが少なく、自然素材ならではの美しさを持つ灯りです。大きく、安定した炎は、古くから寺院や茶室でも大切に使われてきました。
蝋作家・Meria
神奈川県藤沢市を拠点に、Meriaは湘南の自然と地域の素材を生かした「湘南和蝋燭」を制作しています。地元の農家や事業者から届く自然素材を選び、色づくりから成形、仕上げまで、すべて自身の手で行っています。大量生産ではなく、時間をかけて一つひとつをつくること。ワークショップでは、手を動かすうちに時間を忘れ、ものづくりそのものに静かに没頭できる場を大切にしています。

route.title: The Masamune Legacy
route.body: Masamune — properly, Gorō Nyūdō Masamune — is counted among Japan's Three Great Swordsmiths. His work was recorded in the Kyōhō Meibutsuchō , a register of treasured blades commissioned by the eighth shogun, Tokugawa Yoshimune. He is also said to have been admired by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. His Sōshū-den tradition of swordsmithing continues today in Kamakura, upheld by the family's twenty-fourth-generation swordsmith. At the hearth, you will encounter raw steel and the patient discipline that transforms it into a blade.
route.bodyJa: 正宗——正式には五郎入道正宗——は日本三大刀匠の一人に数えられ、その作は八代将軍・徳川吉宗の命により編纂された名物帳「享保名物帳」にも記されています。豊臣秀吉にも愛されたと伝わるその相州伝の技は、鎌倉の地で今なお受け継がれ、一門の24代目がその系譜を守っています。炉端では、生の鋼と、それを刃へと変える忍耐の技に間近で向き合っていただきます。

route.title: The Forge
route.body: At the hearth, steel is heated until it glows, then drawn, folded, and struck into shape amid a shower of sparks. Guests stand close enough to feel the heat and hear the cadence of the hammer, guided through each stage by the swordsmith and an interpreter. This is not a demonstration behind glass. It is the workshop's everyday craft, opened exclusively to a small group.
route.bodyJa: 炉端では、鋼が赤く灼けるまで熱され、打たれ、折り返され、火花とともに少しずつ形をなしていきます。お客様は熱と槌の音を間近に感じられる距離に立ち、刀匠と同行の通訳ガイドの案内のもと、その工程をひとつひとつご覧いただきます。ガラス越しの実演ではなく、工房の日常であり、同時に類まれな仕事を、少人数のためだけに開いていただく時間です。

route.title: Sword Appreciation & Tea
route.body: Following the forging experience, learn haitō — the quiet etiquette of viewing a Japanese sword: how to hold it, how to look at it, and what to notice in the grain of the steel and the line of its edge. The visit closes with tea and traditional sweets, served in the same unhurried quiet that runs through the experience.
route.bodyJa: 鍛錬見学の後は、日本刀を鑑賞する際の静かな作法「拝刀」を学びます——刀の持ち方、見方、そして鋼の地肌や刃文に何を見るか。体験の締めくくりには、お茶と季節の菓子を、体験全体を貫く落ち着いた静けさの中でお召し上がりいただきます。

ledeParasEn: The places you visit, the stories you encounter, and the food. We thoughtfully shape your day in Kamakura around your interests and preferences.

Enjoy a custom private tour with ZENRISE, shaped around your interests and your own pace. Along the way or at the end of the day, take time to savor seasonal ingredients at Restaurant COCON. You can choose between lunch and dinner.

Nestled in a quiet valley in Nikaido, Kamakura COCON is an all-suite auberge limited to just two groups per day. The historic building, originally constructed in 1855, has been carefully renovated while preserving its character. Stone-paved paths, moss gardens, and views of the changing seasons through traditional lattice windows create a sense of stillness within Kamakura.
Highlights of the Experience
Custom Private Guided Tour

Explore Kamakura's history, culture, and quieter corners with a knowledgeable local guide. Your itinerary is shaped around your interests and pace, with a choice of a Half-Day (4 hours) or Full-Day (8 hours) experience.
Seasonal Dining at Restaurant Cocon

Take a seat at the open-kitchen counter and enjoy a seven-course menu followed by two desserts. Seasonal ingredients from Kamakura, Shonan, and across Japan are carefully selected and prepared using Italian culinary techniques.
Choose between lunch and dinner.

route.bodyJa: WITH HARAJUKU前でガイドと合流。

route.title: Walk along Takeshita Street
route.body: Explore shops featuring Kawaii culture, character goods, and the latest Japanese fashion trends.
route.bodyJa: Kawaiiカルチャーとトレンドファッションのショップを巡ります。

route.title: Purikura Experience
route.body: With your guide's support, take your purikura photos and print them on the spot to take home as a unique souvenir.
route.bodyJa: ガイドのサポートで撮影し、その場でお持ち帰りいただけます。

route.title: Shopping
route.body: Browse character merchandise, Kawaii accessories, and Japanese souvenirs.
route.bodyJa: キャラクターグッズ、Kawaiiアクセサリー、お土産のショッピング。

route.title: A Sweet Break
route.body: Take a break and enjoy a Japanese sweet, such as a famous Harajuku crepe.
route.bodyJa: 原宿名物のクレープなど、日本のスイーツをお楽しみいただきます。

route.title: Walk to Shibuya
route.body: Walk from Harajuku to Shibuya and visit the Hachiko Statue, while learning the story behind this beloved Tokyo landmark.
route.bodyJa: 忠犬ハチ公像を訪れ、由来をご紹介します。

route.title: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
route.body: Cross the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing and continue through Center-gai, one of the area's lively shopping streets.
route.titleJa: スクランブル交差点通過
route.bodyJa: スクランブル交差点を渡り、センター街を歩きます。

route.title: Visit
route.body: Visit Nintendo TOKYO and Pokémon Center Shibuya.
route.bodyJa: Nintendo TOKYO とポケモンセンターシブヤを訪問。

route.title: Tour Ends
route.body: Your guide will share recommendations for places to explore after the tour. The tour then ends, and you are free to continue exploring Shibuya at your own pace.
route.bodyJa: ガイドからおすすめスポットをご案内して終了。その後は自由行動です。

ledeParasEn: Anime, gaming, trading cards, and Kawaii culture are among the experiences many visitors hope to discover in Japan.
Yet with the language barrier and so many places to choose from, it can be difficult to know where to go or how to experience them.

With an English-speaking local guide by your side, we help you navigate the area, from choosing the right shops to showing you how to enjoy each experience. Try purikura, gachapon, and other Japanese pop culture experiences for yourself — not simply as a spectator.

Over three and a half hours, walk from Harajuku to Shibuya on a route that brings together some of Tokyo's most recognizable pop culture experiences. Explore Kawaii culture and enjoy a Japanese crepe along Takeshita Street, then try purikura, a uniquely Japanese photo booth experience.
Continue on foot to Shibuya, where you'll visit the Hachiko Statue and walk across the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing. The tour concludes at Nintendo TOKYO and Pokémon Center Shibuya.
With plenty of memorable places to see and photograph along the way, this tour is especially popular with first-time visitors to Japan.

海外のお客様の「日本でやりたいこと」の上位にありながら、言葉の壁と情報量の多さで実際にはたどり着けないジャンルです。
本ツアーは英語対応のローカルガイドが同行し、店の選び方から遊び方までサポート。ガチャガチャもクレーンゲームもプリクラも、見るだけでなく実際に体験していただきます。
原宿から渋谷へ、歩いて回る3時間半。東京のポップカルチャーを一筆書きで巡るコースです。原宿の竹下通りでKawaiiカルチャーとクレープを楽しみ、日本ならではのプリクラを体験。渋谷に移動してハチ公像とスクランブル交差点を歩きNintendo TOKYOとポケモンセンターシブヤで締めくくります。写真に残る場所が多く、初来日のお客様に特に好評です。
